Estimate the effect on the estimand's scale

Source: R/effects.R
pollin_effects.Rd

Reads the estimand's contrast from each fitted model by G-computation: every row of the model data is predicted under the high arm and under the low arm, the predictions are averaged, and the effect is formed from the two averaged predictions. A ratio-type scale is a ratio of averaged predictions, never an average of unit ratios. With rr = high / low:

Usage

pollin_effects(
  fit,
  by = fit$by,
  interval = c("delta", "delta_fixed", "bootstrap", "posterior"),
  n_boot = 999L,
  seed = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  n_draws = 4000L
)

Arguments

fit

A pollin_fit() object.

by

The column the fit was made with, pollin_fit(..., by = ). Defaults to the fit's by, giving one contrast per level from the fixed treatment-by-level effects, each averaged over the rows at that level. NULL gives one contrast averaged over all rows. A column the fit was not made with is an error: refit with pollin_fit(..., by = ).

interval

"delta" (the default for a glmmTMB fit), "delta_fixed", "bootstrap", or "posterior" (for a flexyBayes fit).

n_boot

Number of parametric bootstrap refits, used when interval = "bootstrap".

seed

Optional integer seed for the bootstrap simulation or the posterior draws. Each response is drawn from this seed, and the session's random number state is restored afterwards.

conf_level

Confidence level of the interval.

n_draws

Number of posterior draws, used when interval = "posterior".

Value

An object of class pollin_effects: a list holding table, with one row per response (and per by level) and the columns response, contrast, any by column, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high, p.value, family (the estimand family), scale, basis, distribution (the model family) and interval; and interval, n_boot, seed, conf_level, by, the estimand and n_draws (posterior intervals only).

Details

ScaleBasisEstimate
"difference"eitherhigh - low
"ratio""loss"D = 1 - 1 / rr
"ratio""gain"rr - 1
"rii"either(rr - 1) / (rr + 1), equal to D / (2 - D)
"lnrr"eitherlog(rr)

With interval = "delta", the interval for a ratio-type scale is a delta interval for log(rr), transformed to the scale, so the loss share stays below 1 and the RII inside (-1, 1); its p-value tests rr = 1. The delta interval is taken over the fixed effects and the random effects jointly, with their covariance from the inverse of the joint precision of the Laplace approximation: the estimand averages over the blocks and slopes of this trial, so the random effects enter at their realised values, with their uncertainty and their correlation with the fixed effects. A zero-inflated fit, or one whose joint precision is singular (a variance at zero), is an error that points to the bootstrap. interval = "delta_fixed" is the delta interval of pollinatoR 0.3.1 and earlier, from marginaleffects: it varies the fixed effects and holds the random effects at their modes, so it is wider than the joint interval wherever the estimand depends on both, as on a design with a random treatment slope or under a logit link. With interval = "bootstrap", responses are simulated from the fitted model (new random effects included), the model is refitted to each simulated set, and the interval is the percentile interval of the refitted estimates; std.error is their standard deviation and p.value is NA.

A fit with engine = "flexyBayes" has the "posterior" interval, its default and only one: the estimate is the median of the posterior draws of the estimand from pollin_draws(), the interval their equal-tailed interval, std.error their standard deviation, and p.value is NA. With the same seed and n_draws, the row equals the summary of pollin_draws(fit, n = n_draws, seed = seed).

When the data declare a denominator (pollin_data()), each response is a count of successes out of that many trials, fitted as binomial, and the arm means are expected proportions (successes / trials), averaged over the rows with equal weight whatever their number of trials; the contrast is between those averaged proportions.

The table reports the trial contrast, overall or per level of by. A population declared with pollin_population() is not used here; the population estimand is read with pollin_draws().

See also

pollin_estimand() for the scales and the basis.

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(
  trt = rep(rep(c("Cage", "Open"), each = 10L), 8L),
  Site = rep(paste0("s", seq_len(8L)), each = 20L)
)
d$pods <- rnbinom(nrow(d), mu = exp(3 + 0.3 * (d$trt == "Open")), size = 10)
pd <- pollin_data(d, "pods", "trt", unit = "Site")
ds <- pollin_design(pd, c(excluded = "Cage", open = "Open"), "rcbd")
est <- pollin_estimand(ds, "dependence", "ratio", "loss")
fit <- pollin_fit(est)
pollin_effects(fit)
#> <pollin_effects>
#>   family   : dependence (E2) 
#>   scale    : ratio 
#>   basis    : loss 
#>   estimate : 1 - Cage/Open (loss share) 
#>   interval : 95% delta, fixed and random effects jointly 
#>  response     contrast  estimate std.error  conf.low conf.high      p.value
#>      pods Open vs Cage 0.2688808 0.0439437 0.1774744 0.3501293 1.882781e-07
#>      family scale basis distribution interval
#>  dependence ratio  loss      nbinom2    delta
pollin_effects(fit, interval = "bootstrap", n_boot = 50L, seed = 1L)
#> <pollin_effects>
#>   family   : dependence (E2) 
#>   scale    : ratio 
#>   basis    : loss 
#>   estimate : 1 - Cage/Open (loss share) 
#>   interval : 95% parametric bootstrap (50 refits) 
#>  response     contrast  estimate  std.error conf.low conf.high p.value
#>      pods Open vs Cage 0.2688808 0.03479058 0.210163 0.3186358      NA
#>      family scale basis distribution  interval
#>  dependence ratio  loss      nbinom2 bootstrap
# }
